payload.name: House Money Effect
payload.fact: The house money effect is the phenomenon where prior gains increase an individual's willingness to accept risky gambles, often because the starting capital is perceived as 'windfall' rather than 'normal income'.

provenance.title: Why are gainers more risk seeking
provenance.quote_or_locus: The phenomenon that prior gains may increase people’s willingness to accept risky gambles is named as the house money effect (Thaler and Johnson, 1990

provenance.title: Why are gainers more risk seeking
provenance.quote_or_locus: The pain of losing 100 Yuan allowance is more serious than that of losing 100 Yuan gambling wins. People will typically reject the gamble of 50/50 chance to gain or lose 100 Yuan if the ante is from the “normal income account”, but accept if the ante is from the “windfall account
